instructions: Stir 3 tbsp soy sauce and 3 tbsp rice vinegar together in a small bowl for dipping. Put the chili oil on the table for anyone who wants heat.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet that has a lid, over medium high. Set 12 of the gyoza in the pan straight from the freezer, flat side down, in rows that just touch.
Cook them for 2 to 3 minutes without moving them, until the bottoms are light golden.
Pour 1/2 cup of water around the gyoza and put the lid on straight away. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.

Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the water is gone and the wrappers look a little see-through on top. You're cooking the filling to 160°F, so if you have a thermometer, check one in the middle. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when the filling is firm and there's no pink.
Take the lid off and cook for 1 more minute, until the bottoms are crisp again. Lift them out with a spatula onto a plate, golden side up.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pan and cook the other 12 gyoza the same way.
Serve hot with the dipping sauce and the chili oil.
method_notes: Both read versions brown the flat bottoms in a little oil, pour water around the dumplings, cover them to steam until the water is gone, then let the bottoms crisp again. RecipeTin Eats cooks about 12 at a time with 1/3 cup water for 3 to 4 minutes, and says to add a splash more water and about 2 more minutes when they go in frozen. Just One Cookbook uses 4 tbsp water, adds 1 to 2 minutes for frozen ones and drizzles sesame oil in at the end. Both serve soy and vinegar in about equal parts with chili oil on the side. This one cooks a bag of frozen pork gyoza (bought or home made) the RecipeTin Eats way and leaves the filling and folding out, so it stays a quick snack.
